conversation.content:
Hello, I’m Sarah, a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to help you settle into motherhood and to check on how you’re feeling now that your little one has arrived. We’ll use a short, well-trusted questionnaire called the EPDS—Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—to gently screen for any symptoms of depression or anxiety you may have noticed over the past week. Your answers stay completely confidential, and this is a judgment-free space; whatever you share simply helps us make sure you get the support you deserve.

We’ll walk through 10 questions together. I’ll ask each one conversationally, and you can answer in your own words—no need to worry about numbers or categories. Ready to start?

Over the past seven days, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

(small sigh, then a faint smile)  
I still laugh sometimes—mostly when my partner makes silly faces at the baby—but it feels kind of forced. The little giggles don’t come as easily as they used to, and I catch myself thinking I “should” be happier instead of just letting it happen.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Sometimes I can laugh—like when the baby makes those funny faces while he’s sleeping—but it feels kind of muted, you know? I have to remind myself to enjoy the moment instead of it just happening naturally.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still get little sparks of excitement—like when I plan a stroller walk to the coffee shop—but they’re pretty short-lived. Mostly I’m just focused on getting through the next feeding or the next nap, so the enjoyment part feels kind of dulled.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a few times this week. The baby spit up a ton after I laid him down, and right away my brain jumped to “I must’ve over-fed him” or “I didn’t burp him right.” I know, rationally, babies just spit up, but I still felt like it was my fault. It’s not constant—just little moments here and there—but they sting when they happen.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

It’s mostly when the baby’s asleep—suddenly I’m listening for every tiny sound, wondering if he’s still breathing, or I’ll worry that a normal grunt means something’s wrong. During the day I’ll catch myself running through “what-ifs” about his weight or whether I’m producing enough milk, even when there’s no real sign of a problem. So, yes, it happens pretty much every day, even when everything looks fine on paper.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

A couple of nights this week I’ve woken up with my heart racing and this tight feeling in my chest. Nothing’s happening—the baby’s asleep, the house is quiet—but for a minute I feel like something awful is about to happen. It passes if I get up and walk around, but it’s unsettling.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days I feel like I’m treading water. I’ll finally get the baby settled, look around at the dishes or the laundry, and think, “Where do I even start?” I’m not falling apart, but by late afternoon I’m pretty worn out and snap at my partner over tiny things—then feel guilty for snapping.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

It’s not every night, but probably three or four times this week I’ve lain down exhausted and then my mind just keeps spinning—going over the next feed, worrying I’ll sleep through his cry, replaying little mistakes. I’ll drift off eventually, but it’s fitful, and when he wakes I’m not sure I ever really got into deep sleep.
I have felt sad or miserable

I get these waves of sadness that come out of nowhere—like yesterday, when I was rocking the baby, a song came on and I just started tearing up. It’s not all-day misery, but it hits a few times a day, and when it does I feel really heavy, like I’m missing the “old me.”
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Not really—no full-on crying spells. My eyes will well up, but I blink it away because I’m scared if I start I won’t stop, and then the baby will pick up on it. So I guess I hold it in, but the lump in my throat is there most evenings.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. I’ve felt low, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself. I just want to feel like “me” again so I can be the mom my baby deserves.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 20: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Source: Patient self-report on 10-item EPDS-style questionnaire

Symptoms / Behaviors endorsed  
- Anhedonia: diminished ability to enjoy previously pleasant activities (laughing, coffee outings)  
- Low mood: daily waves of sadness, “heavy” feeling, sense of “missing the old me”  
- Excessive guilt/self-blame for routine infant events (spit-ups)  
- Persistent, intrusive worries about infant safety and feeding despite reassurance  
- Nocturnal panic episodes (2× this week) and generalized daily anxiety  
- Sleep disruption: difficulty initiating/maintaining sleep independent of infant needs; racing thoughts  
- Feeling “treading water,” easily overwhelmed, irritable toward partner, end-of-day exhaustion  
- Tearfulness without full crying spells; fear of losing emotional control  
- Denies thoughts of self-harm

Pattern  
Mood and anxiety symptoms present most days for >1 week, peaking in late afternoon/evening, not resolving with rest.

Screening significance  
Score pattern suggests clinically significant depressive and anxiety symptoms consistent with possible postpartum depression and/or postpartum anxiety. Denial of self-harm reduces acute safety risk; however, functional impairment (household tasks, partner conflict, sleep) noted.

Recommendation  
Continue screening with validated EPDS; consider formal assessment by perinatal mental health specialist to determine diagnosis and level of care.
